title: Vasquez accepts conditional foreknowledge but not that the decrees precede absolute foresight, lest antecedent necessity follow
source_text: XXXIII. Non tamen haec difficultatis istius solutio satisfacit Gabrieli Vasquez. Probat quidem ille quod dicunt authores sententiae modo expositae, Deum antequam decreta sua condat circa actus liberos, per scientiam quandam conditionatam praescire quo voluntas sit inclinatura, & ad quid se determinatura, si ponantur istae vel illae circumstantiae: sed probare non potest quod concedere non verentur, nempe decreta Dei de actibus liberis in Deo priora esse, secundum nostrum concipiendi modum, absoluta praevisione determinationis ejusdem voluntatis. Nam si concedatur Deum quacunque ratione actus voluntatis nostrae praefinivisse, priusquam absolute praesciat quae futura sit voluntatis inclinatio, & determinatio, putat inde oriri necessitatem quandam antecedentem, quae futurorum actuum libertati repugnat.
pass_a_gloss: XXXIII. Yet this solution of that difficulty does not satisfy Gabriel Vasquez. He indeed approves what the authors of the opinion just set out say, that God before he frames his decrees about free acts, foreknows by a certain conditional knowledge whither the will would incline, and to what it would determine itself, if these or those circumstances were posited: but he cannot approve what they do not fear to concede, namely that the decrees of God concerning free acts are prior in God, according to our mode of conceiving, to the absolute prevision of the determination of the same will. For if it be conceded that God by any manner whatever foreordained the acts of our will, before he absolutely foreknows what will be the inclination, and determination of the will, he thinks that from that there arises a certain antecedent necessity, which is repugnant to the freedom of future acts.
pass_b_english: Gabriel Vasquez, however, is not satisfied with this solution of the difficulty. He accepts what the authors of the view just set out say: that before God frames his decrees about free acts, he foreknows by a kind of conditional knowledge which way the will would lean and what it would determine itself to, if these or those circumstances were in place.

What he cannot accept is what they do not hesitate to grant, namely that God's decrees about free acts come in God, according to our way of conceiving, before his absolute foresight of that same will's determination. If it is granted that God in any way foreordained the acts of our will before he absolutely foreknows what its inclination and determination will be, Vasquez thinks there arises from this a kind of antecedent necessity that is incompatible with the freedom of future acts.

lemmas.gloss: what they do not fear to concede

choices.why: Necessity that precedes and so constrains the act, contrasted with consequent or concomitant necessity; kept as technical terms.
